review_cost.rationale: Nothing structural needs rework, but the sort bug and missing error handling mean I would not approve on the first pass: one round of targeted changes.

findings.issue: sortRows indexes rows by column key ("move", "type", "category") but MoveRowData's fields are moveName/moveLabel, typeName/typeLabel, categoryName/categoryLabel, so those columns never actually reorder while aria-sort reports them as ascending/descending. The `as keyof MoveRowData` cast defeats TypeScript and hides the mismatch.
findings.suggestion: Give each column an accessor (e.g. { key: 'move', label: 'Move', value: (row) => row.moveLabel }) or rename column keys to match row fields, and drop the cast so the compiler catches this class of bug.

findings.issue: Any API failure other than 404 throws from the server function; no route has an ErrorBoundary, no catch on createAsync, and no serverFunctions.onError handler, so a transient backend error breaks the page with no recovery UI (and as an unhandled rejection during client navigation).
findings.suggestion: Add an ErrorBoundary around the route outlet in app.tsx (or use serverFunctions.onError in vite.config.ts) with a retry affordance.

findings.issue: The module is a 704-line god data layer: fetch cache, species/generation/type/version-group indexes, and the shaping logic for all five pages live together, and every route depends on it for both data and types.
findings.suggestion: Split into a server-side cache/api client, the shared indexes, and one module per page's data shaping; export the interfaces (HomeData) so routes stop re-declaring shapes (app/src/routes/index.tsx:15).

findings.issue: HttpStatusCode renders after createAsync resolves in routes that render NotFound from null data; a known SolidStart v2 regression (#2229) can send 200 instead of 404 in that position, and the spec explicitly encourages the 404 status.
findings.suggestion: Verify the emitted status in the production build; if affected, hoist the status decision (e.g. set it before awaiting, or use deferStream appropriately) or accept and document it.

findings.issue: The search input's value is managed three ways at once: attr:value bound to params.q, a local signal, and an imperative searchInput.value write inside createEffect (lines 60-71). This is hard to reason about and is the likely source of future input-sync bugs.
findings.suggestion: Pick one mechanism — e.g. value={searchText()} with onInput updating the signal, plus a single reactive sync from params.q — and delete the rest.

findings.issue: The alternate-form cutoff appears as a bare `id > 10000` in four places with no named constant or comment; it encodes a spec rule someone will eventually change or break.
findings.suggestion: Extract `const ALTERNATE_FORM_ID = 10000` next to EXCLUDED_TYPES with a one-line comment referencing the spec.

findings.issue: The style object is computed from props once in the component body rather than in JSX or a memo, so if Solid reuses a badge instance with a different props.name (For reconciliation) the background colour goes stale.
findings.suggestion: Compute the style inline in the JSX (style={{ 'background-color': `var(--type-${props.name}, ...)` }}) so it stays reactive.

findings.issue: API_BASE_URL is read from raw process.env with a typeof guard instead of SolidStart v2's documented env module, which also fails-fast if the module is imported client-side.
findings.suggestion: Use `import { env } from "virtual:env/server/runtime"` (configured via solidStart's env option) or at least centralise the read without the typeof-process dance.

findings.issue: Selects set both a reactive value on the <select> and selected on every <option>, which is redundant and can disagree.
findings.suggestion: Keep value={currentType()} on the select and drop the per-option selected attributes.

summary: A genuinely idiomatic SolidStart v2 app — correct config, query/"use server"/createAsync data flow, and URL-backed filters — with clean components and a well-typed, server-contained data layer. The blocker is a real, cast-masked bug: three of seven move-table columns silently don't sort while aria-sort claims they do. Beyond that I'd ask for an ErrorBoundary, one honest input-value mechanism, and a split of the 704-line data module before this becomes comfortable to own.
